subject: Task 21.11 - Harden the bounded log subject (fix SEC-21.5-02 Cf/Zl/Zp scalars and SEC-21.5-03 host-platform path extraction). Independent test-quality audit of tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs (23 -> 52 cases) and the src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs change.
summary: The 29 new cases are genuinely discriminating and the suite establishes the two fixes. I independently reproduced the pre-fix probe rather than accepting the worker's numbers: in an isolated copy of the tree (/tmp/final-review/test-quality/prefix-probe) whose ONLY difference from the audited tree is src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs restored from HEAD (git show HEAD:src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs, verified still carrying 'using System.IO', 'Path.GetFileName(primaryPath)', and 'Rune.IsControl(rune)'), the committed 52-case test file yields exactly 'Failed! - Failed: 25, Passed: 27, Skipped: 0, Total: 52' - matching the recorded evidence. The failure breakdown is 18 cases for SEC-21.5-02 (the 10-scalar UnicodeNonPrintingScalarsAreRemoved theory, plus NonPrintingRemovalStillRemovesOrdinaryControlScalars, NonPrintingRemovalPreservesOtherCharactersVerbatim, NonPrintingRemovalDoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace, BoundIsAppliedAfterNonPrintingRemoval, WidenedRemovalStillNeverSplitsASurrogatePair, and the 3 NamesThatReduceToNothing... cases) and 7 for SEC-21.5-03 (3 FinalComponentIsTakenOnBothSeparators cases, WindowsStylePathEmitsNoAccountOrDirectoryComponent, and 3 separator-only fallback cases), and every failure message shows the right defect ('movie<U+202E>.mkv' rather than 'movie.mkv'; 'C:\Users\admin\Videos\secret.mkv' emitted whole; 'C:\' emitted rather than the item id). The workspace was never mutated by a probe - the revert lives only in the copies - and the audited tree still shows the same 9 modified files and 411 insertions / 41 deletions, with the focused run green 52/52 three consecutive times. Assertion strength is good: every negative assertion is an explicit Assert.Equal to a literal expected subject plus an independent DoesNotContain, and the third assertion in the removal theory re-derives the Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp predicate from Rune.GetUnicodeCategory rather than echoing the implementation, so a predicate regression fails it. Every negative has a positive control: ordinary Cc still stripped (NonPrintingRemovalStillRemovesOrdinaryControlScalars plus the pre-existing ControlScalarsAreRemoved / EmittedSubjectContainsNoControlScalars / BoundIsAppliedAfterControlRemoval), non-ASCII, decomposed-combining (U+0301), and astral text preserved verbatim (NonAsciiNameIsEmittedVerbatim / NonPrintingRemovalPreservesOtherCharactersVerbatim), whitespace not collapsed (both ...DoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace cases), the 128-scalar bound applied AFTER removal asserted as exactly 128 'a' scalars after 300 removed scalars (which also discriminates a truncate-before-remove implementation, since that would yield the item-id fallback), surrogate pairs never split, and the POSIX component/fallback cases. The URL-shaped SR-15.4-04 case documents the retained behaviour explicitly in both its name and its XML doc and is correctly filed as a non-discriminating positive control rather than claimed as new coverage. Fallback coverage is complete and asserted in D format: null, empty, whitespace, Cc-reduced, separator-only ('C:\', '\\fileserver\share\', '\', '\/'), Cf-reduced, and the dedicated FallbackIsTheItemIdentifierInDFormat round-trip (length 36 + TryParseExact + value equality), so the fallback is not merely a restated constant. The count arithmetic is independently confirmed end to end: HEAD baseline LogSubjectTests = 23 cases; default suite baseline 0/1937/66/2003 -> current 0/1966/66/2032; host-guarded baseline (re-run by me against /tmp/arrtags-14.3) 0/1957/46/2003 -> current 0/1986/46/2032; both deltas are exactly +29 passed / +0 skipped / +29 total. No new or widened skip: the class carries zero Skip attributes and no JellyfinHostFact / SkiaNativeFact / SkiaNativeTheory / PackagedPluginFact, and the default-suite skip set is byte-identical to the HEAD baseline (20 distinct test ids, 66 skips in both). LogRedactionTests is unchanged and 167/167. No golden, RenderVersion, or renderer change. Integration composition holds: LogRedactionTests drives the real call sites through a real capturing logger and asserts per-site 'item example.mkv' with no '/' and no item id, and LogSubject is the single choke point for the subject, so the new extraction is covered by composition at the integration boundary. PASS_WITH_FINDINGS rather than APPROVED because (a) the documented matrix in docs/release/build-and-release.md still states 1,937/66/2,003, 1,957/46/2,003 and 2,024/21/2,045, i.e. it is stale by exactly the 29 cases this task added, and APPROVED is reserved for a documented matrix that accurately reflects the suite - that drift is explicitly owned by task 21.12 ('Corrected release build, full suite, reproducible artifact, and release documentation'), so it is a deferral and not a 21.11 defect - and (b) four LOW findings, none of which is a BLOCKER or HIGH: the SEC-21.5-03 guard only bites on a POSIX-separator host, the two 'DoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace' cases exercise only the collapse half (no case asserts that leading/trailing whitespace survives, so a Trim() regression would leave all 52 green), the over-removal guard omits the Co/Cn/Mc categories that ADR-026 and the code XML doc name as preserved, and no case has a backslash inside the final component after a '/'.

findings.area: coverage / guard honesty (host dependence of the discrimination)
findings.description: The SEC-21.5-03 guard is host-dependent and the suite does not say so. The three discriminating cases in FinalComponentIsTakenOnBothSeparators ('C:\Users\admin\Videos\secret.mkv', '\\fileserver\media\secret\file.mkv', 'relative\folder\Episode.S01E01.mkv'), WindowsStylePathEmitsNoAccountOrDirectoryComponent, and the 'C:\' / '\\fileserver\share\' / '\' fallback cases fail on the pre-fix code solely because System.IO.Path.GetFileName on the pinned Linux host does not treat '\' as a directory separator. On a host whose Path.DirectorySeparatorChar is '\' the same re-introduction of Path.GetFileName would return 'secret.mkv' and every one of those cases would stay green. The tests are correct for the pinned host and for this repository's Alpine/musl Linux build environment, so this is not a gap in what is verified here; it is recorded because the class and the ADR-026 implementation note both describe the coverage as holding 'on the pinned Linux host and on any host', and a future maintainer running the suite on Windows would get a false green for exactly the finding these cases exist to catch.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs:276-315 - the theory's XML doc claims 'on the pinned Linux host and on any host'; no attribute or comment records that the discrimination itself depends on the host separator set

/tmp/final-review/test-quality/prefix-probe.txt - pre-fix Actual values are the whole path ('Actual: "C:\\Users\\admin\\Videos\\secret.mkv"', 'Actual: "C:\\"'), i.e. the defect is Path.GetFileName treating the string as one file name, not a generic assertion failure
src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs (HEAD version, restored at /tmp/final-review/test-quality/prefix-probe/src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs:56) - 'var fileName = Path.GetFileName(primaryPath);'
/config/arrtags-env.sh and build.sh - the pinned build/test environment is Linux (Alpine/musl); docs/release/build-and-release.md documents no Windows test leg
findings.recommended_action: No behaviour change and no new test required. Add one sentence to the FinalComponentIsTakenOnBothSeparators XML doc (and, if useful, to the ADR-026 task 21.11 note) stating that these cases discriminate on a host whose Path separator is '/', which is the pinned host, and that a Windows-side regression is guarded by the code-level absence of any System.IO.Path use in LogSubject.cs rather than by these tests.

findings.description: Both tests named '...DoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace' exercise only the collapse half of the property they assert. NonPrintingRemovalDoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace uses the fixture 'my <U+202E> movie .mkv' -> 'my  movie .mkv': the surviving text has no leading and no trailing whitespace, so 'my ' + ' movie .mkv' proves that the removal does not collapse or trim the interior run, but nothing in the case can observe a trim. I checked every expected subject in the class (all InlineData expected values, all Assert.Equal literals, and the constructed 'a'-runs and U+1F3AC runs): not one has leading or trailing whitespace, so no case in the 52 asserts that surrounding whitespace survives normalization. A regression that added a Trim() to NormalizeFileName, or that appended the extracted component with String.Trim(), would leave all 52 cases green. This is a property the shipped code explicitly claims (LogSubject.cs's NormalizeFileName doc says 'whitespace is not collapsed or trimmed') and that ADR-026's task 21.11 note repeats under 'Preserved properties', so the claim is broader than the evidence. The pre-existing ControlRemovalDoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace has the same shape, so this is inherited rather than introduced, but the new case repeats the name and therefore repeats the overstatement.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs:234-242 - Assert.Equal("my  movie .mkv", LogSubject.Create(ItemId, "/media/Movies/my \u202E movie .mkv")); the expected string begins with 'm' and ends with 'v', so no trim is observable
tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs:112-116 - the pre-existing twin has the identical gap

tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs:141-164 and 166-174 - the only fixtures with surrounding whitespace ('   ', "\t", ' \u0001 ') all take the item-identifier fallback, so they assert whitespace-only rejection, not non-trimming

src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs:90-101 and docs/decisions/ADR-026.md ('The MaximumScalarValues = 128 bound is applied after removal, the single pass still never splits a surrogate pair, and whitespace is still neither collapsed nor trimmed.')
findings.recommended_action: Add one case to NonPrintingRemovalDoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace, e.g. Assert.Equal(" my movie.mkv ", LogSubject.Create(ItemId, "/media/Movies/ my \u202E movie.mkv "));), so the no-trim half is observed rather than asserted by name. No production change is implied.

findings.area: coverage (over-removal guard vs the documented preserved-category set)
findings.description: The over-removal guard covers four categories; the shipped documentation names six. ADR-026's task 21.11 implementation note states that 'Every other category is preserved, including Mn (combining marks), Zs (space separators), Co (private use), Cn (unassigned), letters, and emoji', and LogSubject.NormalizeFileName's XML doc repeats 'letters, marks (including combining marks in Mn), space separators (Zs), private-use (Co), and unassigned (Cn) scalars are preserved'. The only preservation evidence is one Mn scalar (U+0301 in NonPrintingRemovalPreservesOtherCharactersVerbatim and NonAsciiNameIsEmittedVerbatim), non-ASCII letters (Japanese kana/kanji, precomposed e-acute), one astral emoji (U+1F3AC), and one Zs scalar (U+0020). There is no Co (private use), no Mc (spacing combining mark), no non-ASCII Zs (U+00A0, U+3000), and no Cn case, so three of the six categories the documentation names as preserved are asserted only by the code comment and not by a test. The practical risk is small because IsNonPrintingScalar is an explicit four-category allow-list rather than a subtraction, so over-removal would require editing that list rather than a side effect; but the guard is the thing that would catch such an edit, and a future 'harden further' edit that also dropped Mc or Co would be caught for letters/emoji/Mn but not for the rest.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-026.md, 'Implementation note (v1.2, task 21.11: SEC-21.5-02 and SEC-21.5-03)' - the 'Every other category is preserved, including Mn ... Zs ... Co (private use), Cn (unassigned), letters, and emoji' sentence
src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs:90-101 - the NormalizeFileName XML doc naming Mn, Zs, Co, Cn as preserved
tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs:223-232 - the only mixed preservation fixture: 'お気に入り\u202ECafe\u0301 🎬.mkv' -> 'お気に入りCafe\u0301 🎬.mkv' (Mn U+0301, letters, astral U+1F3AC, U+0020 only)
tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs:128-139 - NonAsciiNameIsEmittedVerbatim's four InlineData rows (Japanese, precomposed e-acute, U+0301, U+1F3AC); none is Co, Mc, or non-ASCII Zs
findings.recommended_action: Either widen NonPrintingRemovalPreservesOtherCharactersVerbatim (or add a small two-row theory) with one Co scalar (e.g. U+E000) and one Mc scalar (e.g. U+0903 DEVANAGARI SIGN VISARGA) alongside the existing U+202E being removed, or narrow the wording in the ADR-026 note and the code doc to the four categories that are actually exercised. The test route is preferred; it costs two InlineData rows.

findings.area: coverage (documented consequence of the new extraction is unpinned)
findings.description: ADR-026's task 21.11 note states, as a documented consequence of the new dual-separator extraction, that 'a POSIX file name that itself contains a backslash is truncated to the text after that backslash (a strictly shorter, safer subject)'. No case in the 52 exercises that shape: every FinalComponentIsTakenOnBothSeparators row has its last separator inside a directory chain ('C:/Users\admin/Videos/secret.mkv', '/media\Movies/mixed.mkv', 'relative\folder\Episode.S01E01.mkv'), so the extracted component never itself contains a backslash. The consequence is therefore pinned only indirectly, and a plausible over-removal - an ExtractFinalComponent that, say, also deleted or escaped any residual backslash inside the component, or one that stripped a backslash-prefixed name - would pass all 52 cases while contradicting the note. The security-relevant direction (no directory, drive, share, or parent component ever emitted) is covered strongly by the DoesNotContain('\\') assertions; this finding is about the narrower, documented, lossy-on-purpose consequence.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-026.md, task 21.11 note, 'Final-component extraction (SEC-21.5-03)' bullet - 'a POSIX file name that itself contains a backslash is truncated to the text after that backslash (a strictly shorter, safer subject)'
tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs:284-297 - the five theory rows; none has a backslash after the final '/'
src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs:83-87 - ExtractFinalComponent takes Math.Max(LastIndexOf('/'), LastIndexOf('\\')) with no handling of a backslash inside the returned component
findings.recommended_action: Add one row pinning the documented consequence, e.g. [InlineData("/media/Movies/ac\\dc.mkv", "dc.mkv")] to FinalComponentIsTakenOnBackslashInsideTheFinalComponent, or state the consequence in a comment on the existing theory. If the behaviour is not intended to be contractual, delete the sentence from the ADR-026 note instead - but do not leave the note claiming behaviour the suite does not pin.

findings.area: coverage (reachability of the pinned URL-shaped behaviour)
findings.description: UrlShapedPathRetainsItsQueryUnchanged is correctly framed: its name and XML doc state that the extraction is a path splitter and not a URL parser, that the retained query is unchanged by task 21.11, and that the case exists so the behaviour is neither silently altered nor silently dropped; it is also honestly filed as a positive control that passes pre-fix, and it reproduces exactly the input the task 21.10 review used ('/media/movies/a.mkv?apikey=X' -> 'a.mkv?apikey=X'). The observation is recorded because the case pins, as suite-enforced behaviour, a subject that literally contains the text 'apikey='. That is only acceptable because of an argument made outside this suite: the only value that reaches the subject is MediaLocationSummary.PrimaryPath, built from the Jellyfin host's MediaSourceInfo.Path / item.Path, which on the pinned host is a filesystem path, so no provider URL or credential can reach it (adjudicated unreachable in docs/implementation/15.4/security-review.json SR-15.4-04 and re-confirmed in docs/implementation/21.10/security-review.json under SEC-21.5-03). Nothing in LogSubjectTests or LogRedactionTests pins that reachability premise, so if a future change ever let a provider URL reach MediaLocationSummary.PrimaryPath, the suite would assert the credential-bearing subject rather than fail. This is INFORMATIONAL because the premise is owned by the security review and the live matrix, not by the unit suite, and because the task explicitly asked for this case to document the retained behaviour.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs:349-360 - the case, its doc comment, and the 'apikey=X' fixture

docs/implementation/15.4/security-review.json SR-15.4-04 - 'no provider payload, request URL, or PluginConfiguration field can reach it, so no credential can reach the log by this route', with the optional hardening 'reject a value that parses as an absolute URI before taking the last segment'

findings.recommended_action: No change to the test. If the task 21.14 release security review wants a defence in depth, the recorded option is to reject a component that parses as an absolute URI before emitting it; if that is taken later, this case must be updated in the same change, because it is now a pinning assertion rather than a documentation note.

findings.area: coverage (integration-boundary assertion for the backslash case)
findings.description: The per-site integration helper in the redaction suite excludes '/' but not '\' from a log message: AssertFileNameSubject asserts the message contains 'item example.mkv', contains no '/', and contains no item id. That is the assertion that would catch a directory chain reaching a real call site, and after 21.11 the backslash is the separator that matters. The composition argument holds - LogSubject is the single choke point, ExtractFinalComponent no longer touches System.IO at all, and the unit suite proves no backslash survives - so this is not a gap in what is verified. It is recorded so that the guard for SEC-21.5-03 at the integration boundary is understood to rest on composition rather than on the redaction suite itself, and so a future change that reintroduced host-platform path handling at a call site (rather than in the helper) would not be caught by AssertFileNameSubject.

substitutes_checked: No substitutes exist in the audited class. LogSubjectTests exercises the shipped src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs directly through the test project's ProjectReference; there is no mock, no fake, no in-process stand-in, no reflection, and no pre-built or extracted assembly. Every case is a plain [Fact] or [Theory] over LogSubject.Create with literal inputs, so the assertions observe shipped production behaviour.

No host dependency: the class uses no JellyfinHostFact, no SkiaNativeFact/SkiaNativeTheory, no PackagedPluginFact, and no ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR / ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT / ARRTAGS_NONCANONICAL_GOLDENS gate, so all 52 cases execute in every documented configuration (default, host-guarded, forced-native) and none of the two fixes' verification depends on the pinned host being provisioned.

Integration boundary (helper -> call site -> log record) is covered by composition rather than by a new integration case: LogRedactionTests drives the real coordinator/reader/worker call sites through a real capturing logger and asserts per site that the message contains 'item example.mkv', contains no '/', and contains no item id. Because LogSubject is the sole chooser of the subject and its extraction no longer references System.IO, the new dual-separator behaviour reaches every call site without a separate end-to-end case. Recorded as TQ-21.11-07.

Golden / renderer scope: git status --short tests/ArrTags.Tests/Goldens/ is empty and git diff --stat shows no renderer, RenderVersion, fingerprint, dependency, or configuration file; the only production file in the diff is src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs. No golden comparison can auto-approve a change here because the golden inputs are read-only test inputs and no golden is involved in the log-subject path.
Secret-sentinel coverage is unchanged: LogRedactionTests still drives all sentinels at every verbosity level and passes 167/167, so the log-secret claim for the subject is not weakened by 21.11.
skips_checked: No skip was added, widened, or removed: `grep -c Skip tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs` returns 0, and the file contains no Fact/Theory attribute other than [Fact] and [Theory] with InlineData.

Default-suite skip sets are identical between the HEAD baseline and the current tree: 20 distinct skipped test ids and 66 skips in both runs, and `diff` of the sorted skip-name lists is empty (/tmp/final-review/test-quality/skips-baseline.txt vs skips-current.txt). The 66 are the 20 pinned-host facts, the 45 ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT-gated native-render/decode cases, and the 1 ARRTAGS_NONCANONICAL_GOLDENS-gated cross-runtime comparison, exactly as docs/release/build-and-release.md describes.
Host-guarded skip count is unchanged at 46 (baseline re-run by this review: 46; current: 46), so ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR still unskips only the 20 pinned-host facts.

No shipped behaviour claimed verified by this task is skipped in any documented configuration: both fixes live in a helper that is exercised by unguarded unit tests, so nothing about SEC-21.5-02 or SEC-21.5-03 depends on a host-guarded or native-forced leg. The 66/46 skips are all pre-existing renderer and pinned-host gates that this task did not touch.
determinism_checked: No wall-clock, random, network, filesystem-order, or process-state dependence in the 52 cases: all inputs are inline literals or string.Concat/Enumerable.Repeat over constants, and the only randomness-shaped helper is CountScalarValues, a deterministic rune walk.

All string assertions are ordinal: Assert.Equal(string, string) is ordinal in xUnit, and every explicit search uses Assert.DoesNotContain(string, string, StringComparison.Ordinal) or a char overload. No culture-sensitive comparison is used; the only culture reference is CultureInfo.InvariantCulture on the expected Guid.ToString("D"), which matches production.

Culture independence of the classification is structural, not environmental: both production IsNonPrintingScalar and the test's independent IsNonPrintingRune use Rune.GetUnicodeCategory, which reads the BCL's own Unicode tables and is not affected by the environment's DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1 (set by /config/arrtags-env.sh). The test's restatement is an independent expression of the documented Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp set, not a call into the implementation, so it cannot pass by sharing a bug.

Repeatability: three consecutive focused runs returned 52/52 with 94, 94, and 95 ms; the pre-fix probe returned the identical 25/27/52 signature and the same 25 named failures. The pre-fix probe was executed in a separate copy of the tree, so it is not subject to the shared-working-tree stale-binary hazard recorded as TQ-21.7-01 (each copy was built with dotnet build immediately before its run, and the copies are independent bin/obj trees).

Isolation: the class holds no mutable static state (one readonly Guid and two pure private static helpers), creates nothing on disk, and has no ordering or sharing dependency; the new cases were added alongside, not interleaved into, the existing ones.

No golden or byte comparison is involved in the audited path, so there is no golden that could silently auto-approve changed output; the only byte-level claim in the task (no golden, RenderVersion, or renderer-schema change) was verified with an empty git status under tests/ArrTags.Tests/Goldens/ and a git diff --stat containing no renderer file.
limitations: This is an audit of the tests, not of the production change or of the security disposition of SEC-21.5-02 and SEC-21.5-03; the release security review of the corrected candidate is task 21.14 and owns whether both findings are closed.

The pre-fix probe was run in a copy of the tree at /tmp/final-review/test-quality/prefix-probe rather than by reverting the working tree, so the audited working tree was never mutated (verified: git status still lists the same 9 modified files and git diff --stat is still 9 files / 411 insertions / 41 deletions, and src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs still differs from HEAD). This is a deliberate deviation from the worker's in-place method and is the safer of the two; it does mean the probe exercised a filesystem copy rather than /workspace/ArrTags itself, though the copy is byte-identical except for that one restored file.

The host-guarded leg was re-run against the already-provisioned /tmp/arrtags-14.3 host rather than a freshly provisioned one; I did not independently re-verify that host's Jellyfin.Api.dll product version matches the documented pinned 12+6c073e19ddf604b2369c638716164fdab4c952dc, so I take the worker's provisioning evidence on that point.
